For, speaking of the second covenant in his preface, concerning caring for the soul, he says, “This second covenant was made with Adam, and with us in him, immediately after the fall, and is briefly contained in these words, Genesis 3:15, where God declares, ‘The seed of the woman shall break the serpent’s head’; and this was made up, as the first was, of some mercies to be afforded by God, and some duties to be performed by us.”
This is exceedingly false theology: for those words are not spoken to Adam; they are directed only to the serpent.
Adam and Eve stood by as criminals, and God could not deal with them, because they had broken his covenant.

And it is so far from being a covenant in which “some mercies are to be afforded by God, and some duties to be performed by us,” that there is not a word here pointing that way; it is only a declaration of a free gift of salvation through Jesus Christ our Lord.

God the Father and God the Son had entered into a covenant from all eternity concerning the salvation of the elect, in which God the Father promised that, if the Son would offer his soul as a sacrifice for sin, he should see his seed.
Now this is an open revelation of that secret covenant, and therefore God speaks in the most positive terms: “It shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.”
God had dealt with the first Adam before; he proved false: God therefore, to secure the second covenant from being broken, puts it into the hands of the second Adam, the Lord from heaven.

Adam, after the fall, no longer stood as our representative; he and Eve were only private persons, as we are, and were only to lay hold by faith of the declaration of mercy contained in this promise (as they really did), and by that they were saved.
I do not deny that we are to believe and obey, if we are to be everlastingly saved.

Faith and obedience are conditions, if we only mean that in order they come before our salvation; but I deny that these are proposed by God to Adam, or that God deals with him in this promise as he did before the fall under the covenant of works.
For how could that be, when Adam and Eve were now prisoners at the bar, without strength to perform any conditions at all?

The truth is this: God, as a reward for Christ’s sufferings, promised to give the elect faith and repentance, in order to bring them to eternal life; and both these, and everything else necessary for their everlasting happiness, are infallibly secured to them in this promise; as Mr. Rastan, an excellent Scottish theologian, clearly shows in a book entitled “A View of the Covenant of Grace.”

This is by no means an unnecessary distinction; it is a matter of great importance: for want of knowing this, people have been misled for so long. They have been taught that they must do this and that, as though they were under a covenant of works, and then for doing this they would be saved.

Whereas, on the contrary, people should be taught that the Lord Jesus was the second Adam, with whom the Father entered into covenant for fallen man; that they can now do nothing of or for themselves, and should therefore come to God, begging him to give them faith, by which they will be enabled to lay hold of the righteousness of Christ; and that they will then show forth that faith by their works, out of love and gratitude to the ever-blessed Jesus, their most glorious Redeemer, for what he has done for their souls.

This is a consistent, scriptural scheme; without holding this, we must run into one of two bad extremes, I mean Antinomianism on the one hand or Arminianism on the other: from both of which may the good Lord deliver us!

But to proceed: by the seed of the woman we are here to understand the Lord Jesus Christ, who, though true God of true God, was, for us men and for our salvation, to have a body prepared for him by the Holy Spirit, and to be born of a woman who never knew a man, and by his obedience and death to make atonement for man’s transgression, and bring in an everlasting righteousness, work a new nature in them, and so bruise the serpent’s head, that is, destroy his power and dominion over them.
By the serpent’s seed we are to understand the devil and all his children, who are permitted by God to tempt and sift his children.
But, blessed be God, he can reach no further than our heel.
There is no doubt that Adam and Eve understood this promise in this sense; for it is plain that in the latter part of the chapter sacrifices were instituted.
For where would those skins come from, of which God made them coats, but from beasts slain for sacrifice?
We find Abel, as well as Cain, offering sacrifice in the next chapter; and the apostle tells us he did it by faith, no doubt in this promise.
And Eve, when Cain was born, said, “I have gotten a man from the Lord,” or (as Mr. Henry observes it may be rendered), “I have gotten a man — the Lord — the promised Messiah.”

Some further suppose that Eve was the first believer; and therefore they translate it this way: “The seed (not of the, but) of this woman”; which magnifies the grace of God all the more, that she who was first in the transgression should be the first partaker of redemption.

Adam believed also, and was saved: for the Lord God made coats of skins for Adam and his wife, and clothed them; which was a remarkable type of their being clothed with the righteousness of our Lord Jesus Christ.
This promise was literally fulfilled in the person of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Satan bruised his heel when he tempted him for forty days together in the wilderness; he bruised his heel when he raised up fierce persecution against him during the time of his public ministry; in a special manner he bruised his heel when our Lord complained that his soul was exceedingly sorrowful, even to death, and he sweat great drops of blood falling upon the ground in the garden; he bruised his heel when he put it into the heart of Judas to betray him; and he bruised him most of all when his agents nailed him to a cursed tree, and our Lord cried out, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
Yet in all this the blessed Jesus, the seed of the woman, bruised Satan’s cursed head; for in that he was tempted, he was able to help those who are tempted.
By his stripes we are healed.
The chastisement of our peace was upon him.
By dying he destroyed the one who had the power of death, that is, the devil.
In this way he stripped principalities and powers, and openly made a show of them, triumphing over them upon the cross.
This promise has been fulfilled in the elect of God, considered collectively, both before and since the coming of our Lord in the flesh; for they may be called the seed of the woman.
Do not marvel that all who want to live godly in Christ Jesus must suffer persecution.

In this promise an eternal enmity is put between the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent, so that those who are born according to the flesh cannot help but persecute those who are born according to the Spirit.

This enmity showed itself soon after this promise was revealed, in Cain’s bruising the heel of Abel; it continued in the church through all the ages before Christ came in the flesh, as the history of the Bible and the eleventh chapter of Hebrews plainly show.
It raged exceedingly after our Lord’s ascension; witness the Acts of the Apostles and the History of the Primitive Christians.
It rages now, and will continue to rage and show itself, to a greater or lesser degree, to the end of time.
But do not let this dismay us; for in all this the seed of the woman is more than conqueror, and bruises the serpent’s head.
So it was with the Israelites: the more they were oppressed, the more they increased.
So it was with the apostles; so it was with their immediate followers.
So much so that Tertullian compares the church in his time to a mown field: the more often it is cut, the more it grows.
The blood of the martyrs has always been the seed of the church.
And I have often sat down with wonder and delight, and admired how God has made the very schemes his enemies devised to hinder his gospel become the most effective means of spreading it.

The devil has had so little success in persecution that, if I did not know that he and his children, according to this verse, cannot help but persecute, I would think he would count it his strength to sit still.
What did he gain by persecuting the martyrs in Queen Mary’s time?
Was not the grace of God exceedingly glorified in sustaining them?
What did he gain by persecuting the good old Puritans?
Did it not result in the peopling of New England?
Or, to come nearer to our own times, what has he gained by putting us out of the synagogues?
Has not the word of God mightily prevailed since then?
My dear hearers, you must excuse me for enlarging on this point; God generally fills my soul when I come to this topic.
I can say with Luther, “If it were not for persecution, I would not understand the Scripture.”
If Satan should yet be permitted to bruise my heel further, and his servants should thrust me into prison, I do not doubt that even that would only serve to bruise his head more effectively.

I remember a saying of the Lord Chancellor of that time to the godly Bradford: “You have done more harm,” he said, “by your exhortations in private in prison than you did by preaching before you were put in,” or words to that effect.
The promise of the text is my daily support: “I will put enmity between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.”
Further, this promise is also fulfilled, not only in the church in general, but in every individual believer in particular.
In every believer there are two seeds, the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent: the flesh lusting against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh.

It is with the believer, when his heart is made alive by grace, as it was with Rebekah when she had conceived Esau and Jacob in her womb: she felt a struggling and began to be uneasy. “If it is so,” she says, “why am I like this?”

(Gen. 25:22) In the same way grace and nature struggle (if I may speak this way) in the womb of a believer’s heart; but as it was said there, “The older shall serve the younger,” so it is here — grace shall in the end get the better of nature; the seed of the woman shall bruise the serpent’s head.

Many of you who have believed in Christ may perhaps find some particular corruption still strong, so strong that you are sometimes ready to cry out with David, “I shall one day fall by the hand of Saul.”
But do not fear; the promise in the text ensures the perseverance and victory of believers over sin, Satan, death, and hell.
What if indwelling corruption does still remain, and the seed of the serpent bruises your heel by vexing and disturbing your righteous souls?
Do not fear; though faint, yet pursue; you shall yet bruise the serpent’s head.
Christ has died for you, and in yet a little while he will send death to destroy the very existence of sin in you.

This brings me to show the fullest way in which the promise of the text shall be fulfilled, namely, at the final judgment, when the Lord Jesus shall present the elect to his Father without spot or wrinkle or any such thing, glorified in both body and soul.
Then the seed of the woman shall give the last and fatal blow, in bruising the serpent’s head.
Satan, the accuser of the brothers, and all his accursed seed shall then be cast out, and never be permitted to disturb the seed of the woman any more.
Then the righteous shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father, and sit with Christ on thrones in majesty on high.
Let us, therefore, not be weary of doing good; for we shall reap an eternal harvest of comfort if we do not give up.
Dare, dare, my dear brothers in Christ, to follow the Captain of your salvation, who was made perfect through sufferings.
The seed of the woman shall bruise the serpent’s head.
Do not fear men. Do not be too much cast down at the deceitfulness of your hearts.
Do not fear devils; you shall gain the victory even over them.
The Lord Jesus has pledged to make you more than conquerors over all.
Plead with your Savior, plead; plead the promise in the text.
Wrestle, wrestle with God in prayer.
If it has been given to you to believe, do not fear if it should also be given to you to suffer.
Do not be terrified in any way by your adversaries; the King of the church has them all on a chain. Be kind to them, pray for them, but do not fear them.
The Lord will yet bring back his ark, though at present it is driven into the wilderness; and Satan shall fall like lightning from heaven.
Are there any enemies of God here?
The promise of the text encourages me to defy you: the seed of the woman, the ever-blessed Jesus, shall bruise the serpent’s head.
What does all your malice amount to?
You are only raging waves of the sea, foaming up your own shame.
For you, without repentance, the blackness of darkness is reserved forever.

The Lord Jesus sits in heaven, ruling over all, and causing all things to work for his children’s good; he laughs you to scorn; he holds you in the utmost derision, and therefore so will I. Who are you that persecute the children of the ever-blessed God?
Though I am only a poor youth, the Lord Jesus, the seed of the woman, will enable me to bruise your heads.
My brothers in Christ, I think I do not speak this way in my own strength, but in the strength of my Redeemer.
I know in whom I have believed; I am persuaded that he will keep safe what I have committed to him.
He who has promised that the seed of the woman shall bruise the serpent’s head is faithful.

May we all experience a daily fulfillment of this promise, both in the church and in our hearts, until we come to the church of the firstborn, the spirits of just men made perfect, in the presence and actual enjoyment of the great God our heavenly Father!
To whom, with the Son and the Holy Spirit, be ascribed all honor, power, might, majesty, and dominion, now and forevermore. Amen.
